land.text: Italy as the Kingdom held it at the end of the war (Cliopatria 1945, 289,198 km2), without Istria, Zara and the other lands ceded in 1947

predecessors.note: 'Italy became a republic after the 1946 referendum held on 2 June'; the Kingdom dossier (eu-13) ends in June 1946.

correction.text: Italy without Trieste: the shape stands unchanged for 1946-1953, while Zone A of the Free Territory ('with the city of Trieste, administered by the British and American forces') is not Italian land until 26 October 1954; from 1954 the new keyframe republic-of-italy_1954 replaces it

keyframe_review.note: 288,839 km2 for 1946-72 against the Italy infobox 301,340 km2 (the body text says 301,230): ratio 0.96; the shortfall is outline detail (coastal cells of Puglia, Sicily, Liguria and the Alps are missing) plus the Trieste province. Cliopatria's Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia row holds the two Trieste cells for the whole of 1946-91, which is wrong after 1954. The shape leaves out Istria, Rijeka and Zadar, which the pages cede to Yugoslavia in 1947 (treaty in force 15 September 1947); Cliopatria draws the post-treaty frontier from 1946.

correction.text: Italy with the province of Trieste, Zone A of the Free Territory, back under Italian civil control from 26 October 1954 ('General De Renzi later declared full control over the area at 12:00' on 26 October)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's 1946 shape never takes Trieste back. Zone A is 222.5 km2 (the page); Zone B (515.5 km2) stays under the Yugoslav army and is formalised as Yugoslav by the Treaty of Osimo (signed 1975, ratified 1977).

correction.text: Italy with the province of Trieste

keyframe_review.note: 288,934 km2 for 1973-75, the same 1,072 cells as 1946-72 (the 95 km2 difference is outline noise, not a frontier change). The Treaty of Osimo (1975) formalised the Trieste frontier ('formalized twenty-one years later') without moving it; Trieste is missing as above.

correction.text: Italy with the province of Trieste, within the treaty frontier of Osimo (ratified 1977)

keyframe_review.note: 288,839 km2 for 1976-2023, cell for cell the shape of 1946-72. No frontier changes on any page opened between 1954 and 2023; Trieste is added.

correction.text: Italy with the province of Trieste

keyframe_review.note: 288,839 km2 for 2024, unchanged from 1976-2023; same Trieste correction.

region.text: Italy within its frontier of 1946, without Trieste and the Adriatic lands under Yugoslav administration

ledger.note: 2 June 1946: Italy votes to become a republic. 'Italy became a republic after the 1946 referendum held on 2 June'; the republic won 54 percent (History of the Italian Republic page, which also dates Victor Emmanuel III's abdication to 9 May 1946 and says Umberto was king 'only a month'). The proclamation day is not on the pages opened.

1947: Italy gives up Sazan Island. 'After the war, in 1947, the Paris Peace Treaty transferred sovereignty over the island to Albania'; Italy had held it since 1920. The island is below one grid cell and not in the Italian shape.

region.text: 'Istria, Fiume, Zara, and most of Gorizia and Pola were ceded'; 'Istria, Kvarner, most of the Julian March, and Zara were annexed by Yugoslavia'

ledger.note: 1947: the Adriatic lands pass to Yugoslavia. The treaties 'were signed on 10 February 1947' and took effect on 15 September 1947; Yugoslav troops 'withdrew to their zone' behind the Morgan Line on 12 June 1945 (Free Territory page), and Cliopatria draws this land as Yugoslav from 1946. The 'most of Gorizia' is only a few cells at this resolution. The Koper and Piran cells (Zone B of the Free Territory, 'a small portion of the north-western part of the Istrian peninsula') are taken out of Istria here, as they go to free-territory-of-trieste in the next event (reviewer eu-22-a).

region.text: the Free Territory of Trieste: Zone A, 222.5 km2 'with the city of Trieste' (British and American forces), and Zone B, 515.5 km2 (Yugoslav army)

ledger.note: 15 September 1947: the Free Territory of Trieste comes into existence. 'established on 10 February 1947, by a protocol of the Treaty of Peace with Italy'; 'came into existence on 15 September 1947'. The page names Zone A's city and the two areas, not Zone B's communes; Koper and Piran are the researcher's reading of Zone B.

region.text: 'The Tende and La Brigue valleys were ceded to France'

ledger.note: 1947: Tende and La Brigue go to France; the grid shows barely any change (two cells, one already French in the Cliopatria shape).

region.text: 'The Dodecanese Islands were ceded to Greece'

ledger.note: 1947: the Dodecanese pass to Greece. The islands, held by Italy since 1912, were a British military protectorate after May 1945 (Dodecanese page); they are not in the Republic's Cliopatria shape.

region.text: Zone A, 'with the city of Trieste'

ledger.note: 26 October 1954: Italy takes over Trieste. The London Memorandum was signed on 5 October 1954; 'Italian troops took over on 25 October', and General De Renzi declared 'full control over the area at 12:00' on 26 October. Zone B stayed under Yugoslavia; the Treaty of Osimo (signed 1975, ratified 1977) formalised the frontier.

certainty.note: Italy's frontiers are treaty lines (Paris 1947, London Memorandum 1954, Osimo 1975/77); the Alpine and Adriatic lines are sharp throughout.

notes:
Cliopatria row: Republic of Italy 1946..2024, four shapes, all the same 1,072 grid cells (areas differ by outline noise). The row shares Wikidata Q38 with 'Italian Republic' (1803..1813, the Napoleonic republic): two different states, no merge; Cliopatria reuses the 'Italy' article. Verdicts: all adjust. (1) Trieste: the province (two cells) is missing from the Italian shape for 1946-2024, and Cliopatria's Yugoslav row (socialist-federal-republic-of-yugoslavia, 1946..1991) holds those two cells for its whole life, wrongly after 26 October 1954; the Yugoslav dossier's author should know. The cause may be a coarse outline at the Gulf of Trieste, not a political choice. (2) The Republic lost land in 1947 that its shape already omits (Istria, Rijeka, Zadar, Tende and La Brigue, the Dodecanese, Sazan): the ledger carries the losses with counterparts that carry the matching gains; Cliopatria draws the post-treaty frontier from 1946 although the treaty took effect on 15 September 1947 and the Morgan Line (June 1945) had already split the Julian March.

Not settled with the pages opened: the proclamation day of the Republic (10 or 18 June 1946 is not on the pages), the 1948 Constitution's entry into force (1 January 1948 is on the History page, but the Italy page says only 1948); the day of the Tende and La Brigue transfer; South Tyrol and the Gruber-De Gasperi agreement (page: Italy kept it 'largely thanks to the Gruber-De Gasperi Agreement'); Italian Somaliland as a UN trusteeship under Italian administration until 1 July 1960 (History page; a colony, not in the shape); Italy's colonial losses (Libya, Italian East Africa; Cliopatria rows italian-libya etc. belong to other groups); the presidents (the Italy page does not list them, so no rulers).

Counterparts needing dossiers: free-territory-of-trieste (1947..1954; Cliopatria lacks it; eu-22-x scope names Trieste). Gazetteer names wanted: Tende and La Brigue; Pula (Pola), Gorizia as places; Sazan Island.

The end year 2026 is the current year (the state is alive).
